considered.name: OwnPeakDeferralWithCollateralScarceBorrowing
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(RATIO(dp, MAX(SUB(at, act), dp)), TS_MAX(RATIO(dp, MAX(SUB(at, act), dp)), 5)))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), MAX(SUB(at, act), dp)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Borrowing that is large relative to the firm's stock of pledgeable hard assets must be secured against soft assets or against the reported earnings themselves; when those earnings are supported by an eroded depreciation charge, lender and shareholder are relying on the same overstated numbers.
considered.reasoning: The collateral-scarcity leg delivered α=−3.3% (t=−2.84) in gen 8 when paired with the working-capital accrual, but it has never met the erosion state that now carries the family's alpha, and it is a genuinely different financing dimension from burn intensity, funding tenor and funding source. Both legs share the net non-current asset base as a scaling anchor, which makes the joint interpretation coherent: the same hard-asset stock that is too small to secure the new debt is also the base whose depreciation is being understated.

considered.name: ErodedConservatismWithSoftAssetsOverEquity
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(RATIO(dp, MAX(SUB(at, act), dp)), TS_MAX(RATIO(dp, MAX(SUB(at, act), dp)), 5)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), MAX(ceq, dp))))
considered.hypothesis: The exposure that matters may be a pair of *states* rather than flows: accumulated erosion of depreciation conservatism alongside a soft-asset stock that dwarfs the book equity available to absorb its write-down, with no requirement that anything dramatic happened in the current year.
considered.reasoning: Every signal in the archive has included at least one annual flow, yet the two alpha-richest non-flow constructions — the erosion state (α=−3.9%) and soft assets over the equity cushion (α=−3.4%, t=−3.61) — have never been combined, and a state-only signal would have far lower portfolio turnover than the flow-based family. The known risk is the slope: the soft-asset-over-equity leg had fmb=−1.08 on its own, so this tests explicitly whether the erosion state supplies enough cross-sectional ordering to rescue a stock-only construction.

considered.name: LiquidityCompositionBelowOwnPeakWithBurn
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(RATIO(che, act), TS_MAX(RATIO(che, act), 5)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), SUB(ib, dvc))), DELTA(che, 1)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The cash share of current assets measures how much of a firm's reported liquidity is certain rather than dependent on collection and sale; a firm sitting far below the most cash-backed composition it has achieved in five years has quietly converted its liquidity into accrual-based claims, and doing so while consuming outside capital is the balance-sheet analogue of deferring depreciation.
considered.reasoning: Rather than stacking two normalizations onto the same champion leg, this transfers the single most productive discovery of the search — distance from the firm's own five-year best, which lifted the depreciation lever from fmb −4.51 to −5.37 — onto an entirely different balance-sheet dimension, testing whether "accumulated erosion versus own peak" is a general property of accounting-quality variables or specific to depreciation policy. The corresponding one-year change of the same variable was the weakest quality leg in the archive (α=−1.9%, t=−2.28), so a strong result here would be attributable to the state framing rather than to the underlying ratio, which is exactly the inference the final generation should be able to draw.

critic_notes.rationale: This is an additive rank blend of two canonical published anomalies (Sloan total accruals and the Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net external financing measure) with no genuine conditional structure — SUMRANK gives credit to firms extreme on either leg, so it mostly re-prices known effects rather than testing the claimed joint-overvaluation mechanism.

The multiplicative rank form does encode a real conditional (accrual buildup only when externally levered) that is not simply the sum of the working-capital-accrual and leverage-change anomalies, though the low end of a rank product is economically ambiguous (it pools "low accrual/high leverage" with "high accrual/low leverage"), which will blunt the short leg and should be diagnosed if ls_talpha disappoints.

The expression matches the stated state-dependent hypothesis and is the most economically crisp construction in the batch, but imposing a full sign flip (rather than an interaction term or issuer-only conditioning) asserts that high accruals predict *high* returns among repurchasers — a strong claim the literature does not support — and SIGN discards financing magnitude and is degenerate near zero.

The first component is a literal reconstruction of Sloan (1996) balance-sheet accruals, and the second component's sign is economically contaminated because (dvt+prstkc)/at is a shareholder-yield measure with a documented *positive* return relation that partially offsets the intended external-finance-dependence interpretation, so the SUMRANK composite mixes opposing forces.

The persistence-count construction is genuinely different from the magnitude blends elsewhere in this batch and has a defensible economic rationale, but a six-valued integer signal produces massive ties that weaken Fama-MacBeth slope precision and destabilize decile assignment, and the five-year requirement will materially cut coverage — both must be checked before crediting any result.

This is a rank product of two well-documented anomalies (non-cash current-asset accruals and the Pontiff-Woodgate share issuance effect) and overlaps heavily with the other accrual-times-financing proposals here; worse, raw csho growth is mechanically inflated by splits and stock dividends unless split-adjusted, injecting non-economic noise into the conditioning variable.

By the author's own admission the economic content is identical to the archived AccrualsUnderRefinancingPressure (accruals × short-term-debt-minus-cash), with only a measurement swap (balance-sheet Sloan accruals, `dltr` dropped) to raise coverage — a mechanical re-spec of an existing archive entry rather than a new mechanism, and one whose archived version already showed a −4.24 alpha t-stat with a null FMB slope that this change does nothing to diagnose.

A clean, high-coverage, internally consistent conditional test (high accruals × high total leverage → low returns) that serves as a legitimate controlled contrast against the liquidity-gap conditioner, though the construction is about as plain a rank-product of two textbook variables as one can write and the accrual-times-leverage interaction is close to well-trodden distress/accrual-quality territory.

This is the same channel as the archived PostIssuanceAccrualPersistence with only a lag removed and ranks applied — a cosmetic respecification — and the underlying accruals × net-equity-issuance combination is essentially the published external-financing/accrual composite (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan), so it risks being both a rediscovery of an archive entry and of a known anomaly.

The diagnosis of the prior signal's failure (six-valued indicator count producing massive ties and an unstable sort) is correct and the continuous three-year financing flow is a substantive fix rather than a relabeling, though the resulting construct sits very close to the published external-financing anomaly interacted with accruals and its incremental content over signal 3 is limited.

The ratio design is a genuinely different construction, but flooring the denominator at `dp` collapses every firm with CFO below depreciation — precisely the accrual-hollowed, cash-poor group the hypothesis targets — onto a common denominator, so for that subsample the signal degenerates into a scaled external-financing main effect rather than the claimed joint accrual×financing quantity; the reliance on `wcap` also reintroduces the ~0.11 coverage problem this batch was meant to fix.

This is the batch's only substantively distinct mechanism — within-firm time-series extremity rather than cross-sectional level, with a coherent argument for why cross-sectional ranks may load on FF5-spanned firm traits — and the expected sign matches the expression's direction; the main caveat is that a 5-period TS_RANK is coarse (25 distinct product values) and will lose early-history observations, so coverage and tie diagnostics must be checked.

This is a strictly monotone re-scaling of the archived DebtBurdenPerInternalResource, and the proposal itself concedes the portfolio evidence is mechanically identical, so it is a cosmetic variant whose only content is an FMB scaling diagnostic — useful as a footnote, not as a signal test.

Industry-relative ranking genuinely changes portfolio composition and alpha (unlike the plain rank variant), the sign is consistent with the expression, and it tests a substantive economic question — sector leverage tilt versus firm-level accounting-quality-under-debt — though it remains a refinement of an already-archived construct rather than a new mechanism.

Economically coherent conjunction of stock stress and flow dependence with a correctly signed expression, but the rationale misstates the operator's properties — a low MIN means *at least one* leg is low, so the long leg still pools contradictory states — and both legs are recycled from the archive, limiting the incremental information.

Multiplying by INDICATOR(ib,0) does not "exclude distressed loss-makers" as claimed — it assigns them a value of zero, which places them at the bottom of the cross-section and therefore in the long leg, so the constructed spread contradicts the stated hypothesis and imports exactly the distress-premium confound the reasoning claims to avoid.

Identical legs to the archived AccrualsInLeveredCapitalStructure with MUL swapped for MIN, which yields a highly correlated signal and is precisely the cosmetic operator variant the objective warns against; the justification is also wrong, since MIN pools states at the low end just as a rank product does.

The payout-sustainability channel is the batch's most genuinely novel idea, but the expression is not conditioned on dvt>0, so for the large non-payer population the first leg degenerates to negative accrual-purged profitability and the short leg becomes an unprofitable-firms-levering-up bet rather than the stated debt-funded-dividend bet.

This is a mechanical re-aggregation of three legs already tested in the archive (Sloan-style accruals, the accrual-adjusted debt-burden ratio, and 3-year cumulative external financing) into a nested SUMRANK that implicitly assigns arbitrary 1/2–1/4–1/4 weights, and averaging a leg with alpha-but-no-slope against a leg with slope-but-no-alpha is far more likely to dilute both than to recover both.

The expression and sign are internally consistent and the "fate of the money" framing is a genuine departure from the archive's quantity-based financing legs, but the reasoning's central orthogonality claim is wrong — by the cash-flow identity, financing minus the change in cash equals minus (operating plus investing cash flow), so the leg is essentially a free-cash-flow deficit and remains heavily exposed to CMA and to the same working-capital accrual it is being multiplied against.

The premise is off: the standard accrual anomaly is already measured over the year *following* the fiscal year, so lagging the accrual leg an extra year mostly adds staleness, and the resulting signal is a minor timing variant of the already-tested AccrualsUnderRefinancingPressure with the net-debt conditioner barely changed.

This is a well-diagnosed, minimal-change test of a specific archive failure — holding the accrual leg and operator structure fixed while replacing a cross-sectional financing level (plausibly CMA-spanned) with a within-firm five-year TS_RANK — and it is distinct from the earlier own-history entry, which ranked the leverage stock rather than the financing flow.

The financing-mix framing is a legitimately new dimension relative to the archive's quantity-based legs and the conditional logic is coherent, but the equity-issuance component is close to the well-documented net-share-issuance anomaly, so any result will need to be shown not to be that anomaly plus a known accrual effect.

Debt scaled by its own five-year maximum is a genuinely untried, scale-free capacity-exhaustion conditioner that is conceptually separate from the already-tested leverage-level and burden-level channels, though the reviewer notes a large mass point at exactly 1.0 for any firm whose debt is currently peaking, which will create heavy ties and make the conditioner partly a proxy for debt growth.

This is essentially a horizon re-parameterization of the gen-3 winner, and the archive already answered the same question with ChronicExternalFundingWithAccruals, where 3-year cumulation of the funding leg preserved the FMB slope but collapsed the FF5 alpha (−0.006, t=−0.72), so the expected information gain is small.

A clean, well-motivated source-side ablation of the winning signal whose sign logic is internally consistent, though it edges close to the well-documented net-external-financing/accrual overlap (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan) already probed by PostIssuanceAccrualPersistence, so novelty is modest.

The use-of-funds contrast is a genuinely new asset-side construction, but subtracting non-current asset growth embeds a *bullish* low-investment component inside a leg whose expected sign is negative, so the two halves of the leg pull against each other and the CMA-orthogonality claim is more likely to reverse the loading than remove it.

Conceptually reasonable regime-change framing, but MIN-ing a continuous cross-sectional RANK against a 5-observation TS_RANK (only ~5 distinct values) means the coarse own-history term will floor and dominate the composite, degrading it into a lumpy screen; it is also largely a re-mix of AccrualsWithOwnHistoryFinancingSurge, which underperformed the gen-3 winner.

Introduces a genuinely different earnings-quality lever (industry-relative depreciation rate) that is largely orthogonal to every working-capital accrual leg in the archive, with an internally consistent sign and a sensible industry normalization for technology-determined asset lives; the main residual risk is that low dp/PPE reflects asset vintage or leasing rather than accounting choice.

The conditioning leg's natural return direction contradicts the stated EXPECTED_SIGN — rising payables lowers accruals and is normally associated with *higher* subsequent returns — so a negative result is more likely to be the stand-alone net-external-financing anomaly surviving a noisy, wrong-signed conditioner than evidence for "funding-tap exhaustion."

This is a mechanical three-way intersection of two already-archived signals (UnderDepreciationWithExternalBurn and the working-capital-accrual burn conjunction) sharing the identical burn leg, so it adds no new economic content and risks a thin, unstable extreme decile whose apparent alpha will be a weighted echo of the parents rather than independent evidence.

Differencing the depreciation rate is a genuinely diagnostic change-versus-level test that strips asset vintage, leasing and industry technology from the archive's strongest leg, though the reviewer should be warned that dp/(at−act) falls mechanically when the firm adds PP&E mid-year, so a "rate cut" may partly proxy for the already-priced asset-growth/investment effect.

The composition-share normalization is a correctly diagnosed repair of the gen-4 soft-tilt leg's dead slope (it removes the bullish low-investment contamination while bounding the variable), but the ratio becomes explosive and near-meaningless for firms whose total soft-plus-hard deployment is close to zero, so the result will hinge on how that noisy subpopulation is handled.

The hypothesis is about book-tax divergence but the expression uses txp, a balance-sheet stock of unpaid taxes, not tax expense or deferred taxes, so a low value mostly means the firm pays its taxes promptly rather than that book income is unsupported by taxable income — and the intended construct is in any case a well-published anomaly (book-tax differences / deferred tax expense).

The netting is internally consistent (the clean-surplus equity term adds dividends back into measured issuance, so subtracting dvt legitimately removes payout-funded "burn," modulo the dvc/dvt preferred mismatch) and the mature-payer-versus-cash-hemorrhage distinction is economically real, but it remains a single-term refinement of the archive's best leg with limited upside beyond a clean diagnostic.

A continuous flow-analogue ratio with full cross-sectional support is a substantively different consolidation of the family rather than another MIN conjunction, and the dp floor keeps the denominator well-signed, though the tested prediction should be explicit: the archived stock version delivered a strong ls_talpha with a zero FMB slope, so this design is on notice to reconcile the two metrics rather than repeat that split.

A narrow denominator refinement of the gen-5 champion rather than new economics, but the lagged non-current asset base genuinely removes the mid-year-capex dilution that could make the "policy change" mechanically an investment-growth proxy, so the test is diagnostic and correctly signed.

The five-year TREND is a substantively different construct from the one-year change (slow conservatism erosion versus a discrete accounting event) and attacks the capex confound independently, though it remains the fourth variant of the same leg pair and carries a real coverage cost that must be checked before any result is credited.

This is an aggregation-operator swap with identical economics, and the claim that additive rank pooling is untested is misleading since MUL-of-ranks (used throughout gen 0–2) is a monotone-in-log-sum full-support composite that already spans essentially the same ordering, making this a cosmetic variant.

A legitimate source-of-funds ablation that discriminates issuance-timing overvaluation from generic funding dependence, and it is internally consistent, but it is a recombination of two already-tested legs with a predictable outcome range rather than a new mechanism.

Tenor of the financing behind an active burn is the one dimension the archive has not paired with the effective leg, the conditioner is scale-free and high-coverage, and the sign logic is coherent; the main risk is that maturity shortening was already weak when paired with accruals, so the incremental information may be thin.

An IND_RANK wrapper on one leg of the champion is a robustness diagnostic, not a new signal, and the archive's earlier industry-neutral test (alpha −5.5% → −3.2%) already tells us the expected direction of the answer, so the expected information gain does not justify a generation slot.

A legitimate and diagnostically informative confound test (industry capex cycle) applied to the change rather than the previously-tested level, but it is a demeaning variant of the gen-5 champion with modest upside, and the archive's earlier industry-neutralization attempt (IndustryNeutralDebtBurdenPerCashEarnings) already weakened rather than strengthened alpha.

By the balance-sheet identity the numerator (Δdebt + net equity issuance − Δcash − Δat) largely collapses to −(retained earnings) − Δcash − Δ(non-debt liabilities), so the signal is mostly a repackaged low-profitability/negative-earnings bet rather than the claimed "loss-funding subtype," and subtracting Δat does not orthogonalize to CMA as the reasoning asserts.

Since RANK(NEG(x)) ≈ 1 − RANK(x), the second term equals 1 − MAX(a,b) and the whole expression algebraically reduces to a + b − 1, i.e. a plain additive combination of the two ranks that destroys the very corner-conjunction structure the hypothesis claims to build.

Pooling the two accounting-aggressiveness levers into a single index before conditioning on burn is an economically motivated substitutes-vs-complements test that avoids the decile-thinning of a three-way intersection, with sign and construction internally consistent.

Coherent and continuous-support recombination of two independently strong constructions with a correctly signed hypothesis, but it is an incremental numerator swap on an already-tested ratio, and the dp floor on the denominator lumps all negative-cash-earnings firms together, blunting the intended "per dollar of genuine earnings" interpretation.

Replacing at with LAG(at) in a rank-transformed scaling variable is a near-monotone reparameterization of the existing champion; the alleged denominator "bias" is second-order and this is a cosmetic variant unlikely to produce a substantively different result.

This is a cardinal-vs-ordinal re-parameterization of the already-tested DepreciationRateCutWithExternalBurn/HabitualDeferral constructions rather than a new mechanism, and it swaps the family's conjunctive MIN for a multiplicative weighting while leaving the deferral leg as a raw ratio-change whose denominator MAX(at−act, dp) can be tiny for asset-light firms — so any measured change will be hard to attribute to the stated "magnitude matters" hypothesis rather than to outlier leverage.

Both components (AggressivenessIndexWithExternalBurn, SoftShareOfInvestmentWithExternalBurn) are already in the archive with near-identical statistics (α ≈ −3.4% to −3.7%, t ≈ −3.6 to −3.9), so recombining them via the same SUMRANK/MIN scaffolding is a cosmetic reshuffle whose outcome is almost certainly bracketed by the two existing results.

The proposal explicitly frames itself as the interior point between two already-tested horizons (1-year change and 5-year trend), which is the definition of a horizon re-parameterization rather than a new economic hypothesis, and the anticipated payoff is a marginal alpha/Sharpe trade-off rather than new information about the mechanism.

Scaling burn by book equity rather than assets is a genuinely different normalization that embeds a leverage tilt (and the MAX(ceq, dp) floor sensibly handles thin or negative equity), though it remains a denominator variant of the family's most-tested leg and risks simply re-expressing leverage, which FF5 partially spans.

MAX-vs-average aggregation is a legitimate and internally consistent test of whether the two accounting levers are substitutes, and the expression correctly implements the stated "judged by the worst margin" logic, but it is an operator-level variant of the gen-7 index and the MAX of two ranks compresses the top of the distribution, so the discriminating power may be modest.

This is the batch's most substantive departure — it replaces the burn leg entirely with a creditor-behaviour conditioner, giving a testable "informed lenders vs. optimistic accounting" divergence story that the family has not run, though the tenor leg has twice delivered weak alpha (−1.6% to −1.8%) and the claimed coverage benefit is overstated since coverage is set by the intersection, not the tenor leg alone.

Internally consistent and a genuinely untested cell, but it is the mechanical pairing of the two in-sample-best legs (erosion state and burn/ceq) whose individual partners were already evaluated, so any improvement is likely selection noise from a family that has now been permuted ~50 ways at only ~11% coverage.

This is the most substantive proposal in the batch — the peak-rate depreciation restatement is correctly signed and correctly nested in the denominator (cash earnings less the avoided depreciation charge), it converts the conjunction into a full-support continuous quantity that plausibly resolves the family's slope-versus-alpha tension, and it is not a relabelling of the prior LAG(dp) restatement.

The industry-cycle confound argument is economically legitimate and the construction is coherent, but this is a single-operator normalization applied to the existing champion, i.e. an incremental refinement whose expected gain (the gen-7 analogue moved fmb from −4.51 to −4.66 while alpha fell) is small relative to the multiple-testing burden already accumulated in this family.

Collateral scarcity is a genuinely distinct financing dimension from burn intensity/tenor/source and the pairing is untested, but the proposal's stated virtue — both legs anchored on MAX(at−act, dp) — is actually a hazard, since firms with a tiny hard-asset base are pushed toward the extremes of both legs by construction and the dp floor makes the depreciation-rate leg degenerate exactly there.

The state-only framing with a turnover rationale is the most conceptually differentiated idea here and the sign logic is consistent, but soft-assets-over-book-equity is close to a leverage/asset-composition characteristic likely partly spanned by FF5 loadings and it carried fmb of only −1.08 alone, so the a priori odds of a strong cross-sectional slope are poor.

This is a cosmetic stack of the two normalizations already being tested separately in Signals 1 and 3, adding a third correlated variant of the same champion rather than a new economic mechanism, and its stated purpose — filling a 2×2 cell — is a specification-search exercise that inflates the family's already severe multiple-testing problem.
